nodes.name: Ni foam pretreatment
nodes.procedure: The nickel foam was treated with ultrasound in HCl (5 M) and ethanol solution, respectively, rinsed subsequently with water.
nodes.source_text: Before electrodeposition, the nickel foam was treated with ultrasound in HCl (5 M) and ethanol solution, respectively, rinsed subsequently with water.

nodes.name: Ni_xCo_{1-x} nanocones electrodeposition on Ni foam
nodes.procedure: In a two-electrode system, a piece of nickel foam and a graphite rod were used as the working electrode and counter electrode, respectively. The electrolyte containing X (≤ 1) M NiCl₂·6H₂O, 1-X M CoCl₂, 1.86 M NH₄Cl, and 0.65 M H₃BO₃ with a pH of 4, which was adjusted with diluted HCl and NH₄OH. The electrodeposition was carried out at 30 mA cm^{-2} for 20 min with a temperature of 60 °C. Finally, the electrode was rinsed thoroughly with water and dried in air. The average mass loading was ≈ 10.8 mg cm^{-2}.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The HR-TEM image revealed the layered structure over the as-prepared catalyst, where the outer layer of the nanocones was an amorphous shell of c.a. 8 nm...

nodes.characterization_summary: Depth-resolved XPS revealed core-shell structure of nanocone catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Depth-resolved XPS measurement was also conducted, the results of which revealed that the nanocone catalyst had a core-shell structure (Figure S4, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD showed three characteristic Ni peaks at 44.56°, 51.87°, 76.45° (JCPDS No: 04-0850); Co doping decreased intensity and shifted peaks to lower angles with lattice expansion from 2.032 Å to 2.035 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2a, three characteristic peaks (at 44.56°, 51.87°, and 76.45°) in the Ni-NC XRD spectrum were well consistent with nickel patterns (JCPDS No: 04-0850).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p for Ni_{0.9}Co_{0.1}-NC shows Ni^{2+} 2p_{1/2} at 873.3 eV and 2p_{3/2} at 855.7 eV, shifted +0.2 eV higher vs Ni-NC indicating partial electron migration from Ni to Co; position between NiO (853.4 eV) and Ni(OH)_2 (856.1 eV) indicating coexistence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2c, the Ni 2p spectra displayed four major peaks, including two oxidized Ni peaks (Ni^{2+}2p_{1/2} and Ni^{2+}2p_{3/2}) accompanied by two satellites peaks. Compared with Ni-NC, the binding energies of Ni 2p peaks for Ni_{0.9}Co_{0.1}-NC (Ni^{2+}2p_{1/2} at 873.3 eV and Ni^{2+}2p_{3/2} at 855.7 eV) shifted to higher binding energy by ≈0.2 eV...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Co 2p for Ni_{0.9}Co_{0.1}-NC shows peaks at 2p_{1/2} 796.5 eV and 2p_{3/2} 781.0 eV, shifted to higher binding energy by 0.2–0.5 eV vs Co-NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co 2p spectra also showed four peaks, including two oxidized Co peaks (Co 2p_{1/2} and Co 2p_{3/2}) and two satellite peaks (Figure 2d). Compared with Co-NC, the peaks of Co 2p_{1/2} (at 796.5 eV) and Co 2p_{3/2} (at 781.0 eV) of Ni_{0.9}Co_{0.1}-NC shifted to higher binding energy by 0.2–0.5 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s spectrum fitted to metal-O at 529.8 eV, hydroxide at 531.0 eV, chemisorbed water at 532.0 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The O 1s spectrum of Ni_{0.9}Co_{0.1}-NC (Figure S6, Supporting Information) could be fitted into three sub-bands, including a peak of metal-oxygen bonds at 529.8 eV...

nodes.characterization_summary: C_dl of Ni_{0.9}Co_{0.1}-NC was 5.40 mF cm^{-2}, larger than Ni-NC (4.40 mF cm^{-2}), indicating increased ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl of Ni_{0.9}Co_{0.1}-NC (5.40 mF cm^{-2}) was larger than Ni- NC (4.40 mF cm^{-2})...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman showed Ni^{II}-OH peaks; Ni_{0.9}Co_{0.1}-NC at 525 cm^{-1} (red shift vs Ni-NC 497 cm^{-1}); at 1.30 V blue shifted to δ(Ni^{III}-O) 478 cm^{-1} and ν(Ni^{III}-O) 549 cm^{-1}; I_B/I_S ratio 1.03 at 1.44 V (vs 0.56 Ni-NC) indicating more γ-NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At open circuit potential (OCP) (Figure 4f,g), the peaks of Ni^{II} -OH located in ≈452 cm^{-1} where the Ni^{II} - O of Ni_{0.9}Co_{0.1} -NC (525 cm^{-1}) showed a red shift compared with that of Ni-NC (497 cm^{-1})...

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-UOR XPS of Ni_{0.9}Co_{0.1}-NC shows Ni remained Ni^{2+}, while part of Co^{2+} oxidized to Co^{3+}.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the XPS spectra of the Ni_{0.9}Co_{0.1}-NC electrode before and after four LSV tests were compared. The Ni 2p XPS spectra (Figure 4b) showed that nickel remained in a bivalent state, while the Co 2p XPS spectra (Figure 4c) showed that an obvious part of Co^{2+} was oxidized to Co^{3+}.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-UOR SEM shows Ni_{0.9}Co_{0.1}-NC maintained original morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the SEM images and XRD spectra of the electrode after the UOR showed that the Ni_{0.9}Co_{0.1} NC maintained original morphology and composition (Figures S18 and S19, Supporting Information).

nodes.evidence_snippet: the SEM images and XRD spectra of the electrode after the UOR showed that the Ni_{0.9}Co_{0.1} NC maintained original morphology and composition (Figures S18 and S19, Supporting Information).
